title: Changing AI model mid-development?
author: Eshinio
selftext:
So I just saw that Opus 5.5 has been released, being near Fable in quality but with much lower cost. I am currently working on a game project where I use GPT Astra as planner/orchestrator and Sonnet 5 as the workhorse doing the code. I currently have a very long chat window with Sonnet 5 since the project started, but if I now change the model to Opus 5.5, will this have a negative impact somehow? Or will the model be able to pick up on what has been going on and made so far?

Have not really tried that before, so just wanted to see if there was some good practices to do before making a change like that.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
Long chat windows / long-running chats are incredibly inefficient. You are already doing something that has a negative impact. 

End your chat and keep the chats short. You can swap models whenever you want. Keep context outside the chat, like in memory, in documents in your repo, or in a task manager.

replies.author: Eshinio
replies.body: So if I end the chat, do I need it to make like a handoff document that I can give to the new chat to restore knowledge or does it figure it out by itself by just having access to the project folder?

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body: Yes, make the handoff. Or you can copy/paste messages out.

replies.author: KitchenPoltergeist
replies.body: There's no longer need to keep chats short. Compaction is much better now than it was at the beginning of the year. I would recommend you just keep going in one session. The value you get from giving them all the context from before is immense.

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body: You’re not getting all the context from before. You’re just getting what compaction keeps.

comments.author: Hot_Professional8287
comments.body:
Yes, you need to be able to change models freely. If you have ONLY had your project context in the chat window, then it's being effectively forgotten by compaction. You need to download a free documentation tool like Obsidian to ward off "context rot" for long running projects.   
  
Seriously do that. Nothing sucks more than outlining a detailed system for a week and then having the agent start hallucinating details as the system you were building slides through your fingers like sand.

replies.author: Eshinio
replies.body: So far I have the agents make and update .md files at all big decisions and when I plan out important gameplay systems etc. Everthing that has been made and decided so far are written in .md files in the project directory. Is this enough, or you still recommend Obsidian?

replies.author: Hot_Professional8287
replies.body:
Yeah that's enough, and you really don't need to worry that much about switching models (especially to a more intelligent model). They generally understand that their job is to build coherently in an existing project. The only risk is with sub-agents, or cheaper models, but even then, if they're given a clear specification/design reference, it's fine. If you're swapping operations between frontier models (Opus, Astra, Fable, Sonnet), then you're great. If you continue to run design through high-end frontier like Astra/Fable/Opus and delegate work to Terra/Sonnet, then you're still good.

I still really recommend Obsidian (it's all .md, too), it's just a great frontend and way to organize markdown.  
  
In summary, you're fine. You have no reason to be concerned about swapping between frontier models

comments.author: vlad_h
comments.body:
I’d switch models, but I wouldn’t switch in the middle of that giant conversation.  
Not because Opus 5.5 can’t read the existing context. It can. The problem is that you’re asking a different model to reconstruct months of accumulated decisions, assumptions, corrections, exceptions, and intent from a giant pile of conversation. Even if it technically has the context, there’s no guarantee it interprets that context the same way Sonnet did.  
More importantly, I’d question why the project depends on that conversation in the first place.  
I’ve ended up with almost exactly the workflow you describe: a stronger model for planning/orchestration and cheaper models doing most of the implementation. But I’ve moved as much project state as possible out of the conversation and into the repo: design docs, contracts, decisions, issues, tests, agent instructions, etc.  
The conversation is disposable. The project state isn’t.  
There’s an economic reason for doing this too. Huge conversations get increasingly expensive because you keep dragging all that historical context through subsequent turns. You’re paying tokens for history that may or may not still be relevant, while also making the model sift through more noise to figure out what matters now.  
So I’d absolutely try Opus 5.5. I just wouldn’t “continue the Sonnet conversation with Opus.”  
Start a fresh session. Give it the repo and a small, explicit handoff telling it where the authoritative design, current state, decisions and next task live. If Opus can pick the project up from that, great. If it can’t, that tells you something useful: too much of your project knowledge still exists only inside the old chat.  
I actually built AgentKit around a lot of this thinking. The goal is to make the agent replaceable: Claude today, Codex tomorrow, local model next week, whatever comes after that. The model shouldn’t *be* the project memory.  
That also makes model economics much easier to exploit. When a better/cheaper model appears, you don’t have to ask, “Can I safely move my six-month conversation over?”  
You just point the new worker at the job.

comments.author: EC36339
comments.body: You shouldn't have long chat sessions and rely on sessions context for storage. Just have it write down everything and put that stuff into GIT so you don't lose it.

comments.author: TonyZwilde
comments.body: Focus more on the context and less in the models. Doc the systems of your game, the decisions, overall repetive instructions and rules that you use, that the model change will not impact your progress

comments.author: Fyren85
comments.body:
If you plan a game let the agent split everything into milestones in a milestone.md. then use a new chat for every milestone. If a milestone is finished let it write into the milestone.md that it is completed, otherwise you would need something like a project_status.md too. One file is much better.

With such a system everything is more sorted. With one big chat the ai gets confused and can't remember things.

And use github desktop for every milestone too if you need to reset something

comments.author: Exhales_Deeply
comments.body:
Are you still using the chat interface for this? That's incredibly inefficient if so. If you use a harness you can use as many models as you want.

If i'm misreading you, though, the point stands: have a living plan document and pull pieces (art design, assets, gui, sfx, music, individual systems) into separate streams and you can choose who does what. then you or any model you see fit can audit and edit the plan and you don't need your gfx swarm to know anything about your music or control inputs (until you want them to)

replies.author: Eshinio
replies.body: I only just switched from Claude Desktop to Claude Code when Opus 5.5 came out, but yes, I was using Desktop until then. I did however have a process of using sub-agents as a dev team, one working in Blender, one working in Unity, one doing QA and then the Lead who manages them and delegates my ideas and requests for the game. Documents are saved by the agents constantly with every change, script, feature or decision being made. It worked well on Claude Desktop but Claude Code seems to be faster, so I'm happy with the change.

replies.author: Exhales_Deeply
replies.body: nice, sounds like you're ahead of the game. I think your main q has been addressed so i'm looking forward to seeing what you come up with :)
